title: Data-informed learnings from a CrazyGames Basic Launch
author: StrangeFableGames
selftext:
Around Halloween I launched my indie game on itch.io: ***What Sleeps Above***, a dark fairytale reimagining of Jack and the Beanstalk. Despite my self-marketing attempts, it still was averaging only around 5 players a day.

Last week it entered CrazyGames' Basic Launch, a week-long trial where they test the game with real traffic. In six days it's had over 1,000 players, roughly **35x the traffic** I was getting on itch.

Other than the thrill of seeing real people play my game, it has been super interesting finally having enough data to spot where players get stuck or quit.

**Some things I found:**

\- About a third of players who quit in the first minute never got past the opening story card.

\- Nearly half of mobile players reaching the first boss got stuck on a swipe tutorial. Turns out they were either swiping the wrong side of the screen, or tapping. Allowing swipes anywhere and adding a looping finger animation  (on inactivity) fixed it, and average mobile playtime roughly doubled from 3:30 to 6:30.

\- A new thumbnail improved click-through from 1% to 1.3%, bringing in roughly 45-50% more players.

\- Smaller fixes to dialogue, death screens and tuning down first boss difficulty also helped.

Claude AI made it possible to iterate quickly. I'd check the analytics in the morning, identify a problem, and often have a tested fix live that day. I shipped eight versions in a week, which would've taken me much longer otherwise.

It's still a work in progress and CrazyGames has a much more casual audience than itch, so getting people through the opening of a slow-burn horror game without watering down my design intent is proving tricky. Desktop day-1 retention improved from 1.1% to 4.1%, but playtime and conversion still need work. I'll likely need another Basic Launch.

It's been a pretty eye-opening week filled with rapid fire analysis and iteration. Having actual player data has changed how I approach polishing the game, especially when small usability fixes can make such a big difference.

Happy to answer any questions about the process or analytics.

The game, for those interested: [https://strangefablegames.itch.io/what-sleeps-above](https://strangefablegames.itch.io/what-sleeps-above)
